## What this session actually did

Three questions were asked of the archive rather than of the literature, and
the answers are what the night produced.

**Mid-generation signals for overthinking.** About forty records bear on this;
they sort into five families (trial-answer confidence, hidden-state probes,
entropy, lexical/behavioural markers, answer convergence). Two are deployable
and three are not, and the reason turned out to be shared. That became
`finding:11877d6cb7defd0d`: a signal predicts only when it carries temporal
structure. It is filed against six papers including the one that contradicts
the intuition hardest — *Amplified Does Not Mean Predictive*, where expressed
uncertainty carries negative Lift.

**Analyses of overthinking behaviour inside the trace.** About twenty records,
in four methodological groups: hand-read failure taxonomies, length-accuracy
dissections, causal interventions (only three papers), and benchmark-anchored
studies. The thinnest part is agentic evidence — one paper, with the largest
effect size of any of them (R² = 0.892), and nothing reproducing it. That is
now queued as `synthesis__q-85150997e2cfc3ad`.

**A staged argument built from both.** Written into
`wiki/topics/overthinking.md` below `<!-- auto:end -->`, declared at 21
sources. It asks whether allocation tracks difficulty or presentation, walks
six stages of archive evidence, and concludes that the deficit is in the
signal allocation is conditioned on rather than in the ability to allocate —
because the decision is fixed at read time, when only presentation is
available. Three predictions it makes are checked against the archive and
hold; five things that would overturn it are listed with it.

The section is the first here to carry an `analysis-sources` marker, so render
will report it stale once the evidence doubles.

## Two things a later session should pick up

**The arXiv listing fallback works, and files papers without a date.** Today's
run fired it 22 times and collected four papers, which settles the question
left open when `openreview` was disabled. But a listing carries no
announcement date, so all four records have an empty `published` field and
render filed their pages under `archive/papers/unknown/`. Harmless for now;
wrong in a year's archive.

Two of the four bear directly on the argument written tonight and should be
read before it is trusted further: *$R^3$-Bench: LLMs Struggle with
Resource-Rational Reasoning under Shared budget* and *Learning When to Think:
Adaptive Reasoning for Test-Time Compute Allocation*.
